text:
ops-bot: Paging: SEV-2 - streaming p99 spike detected in us-west-2, affected service=runtime-streaming, metric=p99_latency, breach_threshold=1200ms, current=2350ms :rotating_light:
casey: oncall here, ack. pulling up dashboards and logs.
casey: @marin @tao can you triage infra side? looks like a node-level degradation alert correlated with ECC counters.
marin: on it, starting node list for the cluster pool serving streaming.
tao: grabbing routing info and current fallback policies.
casey: support, do we have any customer-reported impact yet?
support: one support ticket from a high-throughput partner showed timeouts around 11:02 PDT, they saw partial streaming frames drop.
casey: ok, prioritize live mitigation. preliminary hypothesis: a GPU host is intermittently throttling/producing ECC correctable errors leading to KV cache stalls and tail latency.
marin: found node gpu-34 with rising corrected ECC count and thermal throttle counters. pulling kernel logs.
marin: ```
$ ssh gpu-34
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,temperature.gpu,clocks.sm,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv
index, temperature.gpu [C], clocks.sm [MHz], utilization.gpu [%], memory.used [MiB]
0, 93, 540, 87, 21234
```
marin: kernel log snippet: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, class=0x00000008, ch 00010000, subcode 0x00ec" and repeated ECC corrected messages.
casey: thanks. tao, can we shift traffic away from that node and enable fallback?
tao: yes. executing cordon+drain and routing change.
tao: ```
# cordon & drain
kubectl cordon gpu-34
kubectl drain gpu-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# adjust routing
rtr route update --pool streaming-pool-usw2 --remove-node gpu-34
rtr route update --pool streaming-pool-usw2 --fallback-policy reduce-batch
```
tao: drain returned pods staged for eviction, streaming router detecting fewer active workers.
casey: handing to marin for post-drain validation. @henry can you open a hardware ticket and look at replacement/diagnostics? looks like possible flaky GPU.
henry: on it, I'll request a swap and physical inspection. noting corrected ECC counts imply ongoing memory errors. scheduling hot-swap if counts rise further.
marin: node drained, router successfully shifted ~7% of streaming traffic to warm spare capacity, p99 dropped to ~980ms in the last 30s. still above target but trending down.
casey: good. what's p95?
marin: p95 at 210ms, normal. p99 is the outlier tail from the affected KV-backed sessions.
support: notifying the partner of mitigation and potential impact window (~20-40 min).
julia: product here — which customers might see degraded throughput? any high-availability customers on that pool?
casey: partner we mentioned, plus some small internal sandbox tenants. no enterprise Dedicated clusters affected.
marin: quick check of cache state: some KV entries were evicted during stalls, causing rehydration penalties. we pushed a temporary cache-warm policy for critical prefixes.
marin: ```
# quick check
rtr cache stats --pool streaming-pool-usw2 --prefix /kv/
miss_rate: 12.4% -> now 4.1% after warm
avg_rehydrate_ms: 420 -> 95
```
casey: nice. tao, keep fallback reduce-batch in place until we confirm stability. also enable on-the-fly model-variant fallback for streaming less than 1.2s SLO.
tao: done: routing shows fallback active to model-compact-1 (quantized) for new sessions; existing sessions draining.
henry: hardware ticket #HW-2234 opened, engineer assigned, plan to reseat GPU and run ECC diagnostics. will update ETA in 15m.
casey: incident timeline so far: detection 11:01, page 11:02, mitigation (drain+route) started 11:04, visible p99 improvement 11:05-11:06. continuing to monitor for recurrence.
marin: putting a watch on corrected ECC delta every 30s and thermal. if corrected ECC increases by >100 in 10m, auto-evacuate pool nodes and escalate to SEV-1.
marin: ```
watch -n 30 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.error.corrected,temperature.gpu --format=csv -i 0'
```
casey: what's the user-visible window we're communicating? support, craft a short message: "We experienced elevated tail latency in streaming in us-west-2 from 11:01–11:06. Traffic was shifted away from an impacted GPU host and normal tail latencies resumed; we're doing hardware follow-up."
support: draft ready and sent to affected partner; they're OK with updates.
tao: monitoring dashboards show p99 stabilized ~300ms for last 2 minutes. streaming throughput unaffected after reroute.
casey: good. leaving reduced batch policy and model-compact fallback for 30 more minutes, then we'll test reintroducing nodes one-by-one. marin, coordinate safe rejoin once HW signoff.
marin: will only reintroduce node after ECC delta flat for 30m and thermal stable <85C, plus hwops reseat check.
henry: running memtest and ECC stress now; estimated run 20m. will report anomalies.
casey: after-action notes / action items:
- hardware ops: full diagnosis and replace GPU if ECC continues to climb (henry)
- infra: add automatic eviction rule for corrected ECC threshold (marin)
- runtime: add fallback that reduces batch size earlier on thermal events (tao)
- support: send follow-up summary to customers after incident close (support)
casey: adding this thread to postmortem later. marking as mitigated but monitoring.
ops-bot: Incident update: SEV-2 -> mitigated, watchlist active.
casey: closing handoff to monitoring watch. if we see another spike, page SRE lead. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
